processing: Carefully selected leaf is fixed, rolled and pan-fired into a stir-fried green (chao qing).
harvest_season: Not documented in detail; as with other Yunnan greens, the spring picking is the one to look for.
appearance_dry: Even, straight and heavy strips of a silver-grey colour with well-matched tips.
appearance_wet: Not documented; pan-fired Yunnan greens typically open into even green leaves.
taste_profile: Mellow fragrance over a thick, full taste with a returning sweetness.

brewing.notes: General advice for pan-fired Yunnan greens: water a little off the boil, and shorten the steep if the full taste tips into bitterness.

vintage_note: Sold as a green tea of the current year, as is usual for its class, and best within about a year. Yunwu, cloud and mist, is used for teas all over China, so the word Yuanyang and the maker are what identify this one.
description:
Yuanyang Yunwu is a cloud-and-mist green from Yuanyang county in Honghe prefecture, southern Yunnan, a county better known abroad for its rice terraces. The upper valley of the Zhena River, with its stacked ridges, is an important growing area.

The leaf is fixed, rolled and pan-fired, ending up as straight, heavy strips of an unusual silver-grey with even tips.

The cup is clear green, mellow in scent and fairly thick in taste, with sweetness coming back after the swallow. Use water just off the boil and watch the time, as with any full-bodied Yunnan green.

The silver-grey look is the thing to check when buying. Little else about grades or makers is on record, so ask about the garden and the picking date.
history: Little is documented about when the tea was first made or by whom. Local descriptions treat it as a speciality of Yuanyang county and place its main growing area on the upper Zhena River, a tributary of the Yuan River.
